A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same T-FAKE research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original landmarking results on CHARLOTTE and 300W, thermalization results, and regularization, training-data and inference ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a FAKE-only landmarking control on 300W.

M1.justification: The losses, architectures and label adaptation remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 5.1 describes selecting the landmark with the smallest predicted standard deviation, whereas v3 selects the window with the smallest average standard deviation. v3 Appendix B.2 retains the earlier wording, leaving an actual inference change versus a documentation correction unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FAKE, T-FAKE, SEJONG, CHARLOTTE, 300W, TUFTS and DRIVE-IN in the same training or evaluation roles, including the existing temperature and pose scenarios. The added 300W control introduces no new coverage. Neither version evaluates semantic segmentation.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds FAKE-only GLL+SW to the 300W comparison; corresponding v2 Table 3 contains MediaPipe, FA, Star and the multimodal model. CHARLOTTE and thermalization comparator membership is unchanged after matching renamed entries such as Aachen/DAN and TFW/YOLO5Face.

E3.justification: The 300W evaluation adds an explicit RGB-only training control alongside mixed RGB-plus-thermal training. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets and thermalization evaluation settings remain unchanged. Table 8's revised thermal-only training-data label agrees with v2's existing ablation description and does not establish a changed training procedure.

E4.justification: The added 300W control directly tests whether including T-FAKE harms RGB landmarking, extending the existing training-modality analysis beyond CHARLOTTE. The regularizer grid, cold/warm comparison, inference ablation, generalization examples and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report FID means and standard deviations over five subsets in Appendix A.6 and Tables 6–7, with the same seed-related statement. No repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is added. Landmark uncertainty and confidence thresholds already existed in v2.

E6.justification: v3 Table 4 newly reports FAKE-only 300W NME values of 0.0570, 0.0494 and 0.0874 for Full, Common and Challenging. The multimodal values remain 0.0522, 0.0468 and 0.0743. Existing CHARLOTTE, thermalization and appendix numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) adds the missing infimum over transport plans before the expanded Wasserstein transport-cost sum, correcting the displayed definition. The other mathematical formulations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly includes segmentation masks in its contribution list and broadens the conclusion's dataset claim to thermal landmarking and segmentation. Its abstract and conclusion also foreground thermalization quality. These refinements use content already present in v2; the principal dataset, loss and sparse/dense-landmarker claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds a radiometric-calibration error caveat and revises the interpretation of ground-truth bounding-box advantages. Section 5.3 also broadens superiority wording to Star without corresponding numerical changes. Appendix F's discussion of thermal-screening applications and risks is removed, while Appendix E's principal technical limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly describes subsampled patch distributions and random patch batches in Section 3.1 and Appendix A.2. Table 1 additionally explains the unsuccessful ARL-VTF data request. Most implementation details and the project link are retained; negative texture examples newly mentioned in the main text already appeared in v2 Appendix B.2.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Attention Mesh reference and cites the retained MediaPipe framework paper for that table entry. Related Work changes Aachen's architectural description from dlib to DAN and emphasizes combined face detection and landmark evaluation. The broader literature coverage and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites throughout the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion and conclusion, plus GLL+SW terminology and revised affiliation text. The main section order and most technical appendix prose remain intact, apart from removal of Appendix F.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively reformatted with different typography, margins, title/abstract layout and figure/table placement. v2's duplicated opening figure becomes one figure; Table 1 gains an Out-of-Lab column, the 300W table gains training-data information and a control row, and thermalization rows are reorganized. Retained figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new 300W control strengthens support for preserving RGB performance, and reorganized displays remove duplication. However, v3 introduces inconsistent inference descriptions between Section 5.1 and Appendix B.2. Its expanded claim of outperforming Star at threshold 6e-4 is also unsupported as stated: Table 2 assigns Star zero failures by design using ground-truth boxes, while GLL+SW has positive failure rates on every split. These gains and unresolved reporting problems prevent a confident judgment of net improvement.
